organs.human_name: Compute(): timeChange >= SampleTime gate; SetTunings: ki = Ki * SampleTimeInSec, kd = Kd / SampleTimeInSec; SetSampleTime rescales ki and kd by the ratio
organs.mechanism: Compute returns without acting unless at least SampleTime milliseconds have passed since the last computation; because the period is fixed, the integral gain is multiplied by it and the derivative gain divided by it once at tuning time, so the loop body has no dt arithmetic; changing the sample time rescales the two gains by the ratio so the user's Ki and Kd keep their meaning
assumptions: a fixed period is achievable on the target (the loop is called more often than the period); pre-scaling is cheaper than per-call division on an 8-bit micro
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a loop body of a dozen operations with correct units
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: if the loop is called less often than SampleTime the period is whatever the caller gives, and the pre-scaled gains are then wrong (the library does not measure the actual dt)
organs.human_prior: discrete PID with a fixed period (any controls textbook)
organs.source_boundary: the gate and the two rescalings

organs.human_name: Compute(): outputSum += ki * error; clamp outputSum to [outMin, outMax]; SetOutputLimits re-clamps outputSum when limits change
organs.mechanism: instead of summing the error and multiplying by Ki at output time, the integral term is accumulated already multiplied (so retuning Ki does not jump the output) and is clamped to the same limits as the output; when the actuator saturates the accumulator cannot grow past the limit, so there is no wind-up to unwind; the final output is clamped again after adding the P and D terms
assumptions: an actuator at its limit cannot benefit from a larger integral; clamping the term itself is simpler than back-calculation
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no overshoot after saturation; retuning without a bump
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: clamping the sum to the output limits (not to limits minus the P term) means the sum can sit at the limit while the P term pushes the output beyond, which the final clamp absorbs
organs.human_prior: clamping anti-windup (Astrom & Hagglund); the 'accumulate ki*error' trick is the library's blog series

organs.human_name: Compute(): dInput = input - lastInput; output -= kd * dInput; if (!pOnE) outputSum -= kp * dInput; P_ON_E vs P_ON_M (pOnE)
organs.mechanism: the derivative term uses the change in the measured input, not in the error, so a step in the setpoint produces no derivative spike (derivative kick) while disturbances are still differentiated; with proportional-on-measurement the P term too is accumulated as -kp * dInput into outputSum (integrating the negative of the measurement's change), which removes the proportional jump on setpoint changes for processes where that is wanted
assumptions: setpoint changes are steps chosen by the user, disturbances are not; only the latter should be differentiated
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: smooth response to setpoint changes with the same disturbance rejection
organs.human_prior: derivative on measurement is standard practice; P-on-M is the 2017 addition (the blog's 'Introducing Proportional on Measurement')
organs.source_boundary: the dInput lines and the pOnE switch

organs.human_name: SetMode / Initialize(): outputSum = *myOutput; lastInput = *myInput; clamp; SetControllerDirection negates the gains in place
organs.mechanism: when the mode switches from manual to automatic the integral accumulator is set to whatever the output currently is (so the first automatic output equals the last manual one) and the derivative memory to the current input (so no spurious derivative); reversing the controller direction negates the three gains rather than the error
assumptions: the operator's manual output is the right starting point for the integral
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no jump at hand-over, the property industrial controllers advertise

organs.mechanism: every instruction is a fixed-size opcode from a table; nop-A/B/C do nothing when executed but MODIFY the instruction before them (which register ?BX? means) and, in sequence, spell a LABEL that other instructions read by scanning the following nops (ReadLabel); so the same three symbols are the argument system and the addressing system, and every mutation lands on a legal instruction
organs.input: the genome as a sequence of opcodes
assumptions: a closed alphabet where every string is a valid program (no syntax errors) is what makes random mutation productive rather than fatal
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: mutational robustness by construction; labels give position-independent addressing so insertions and deletions do not break jumps
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a mutation inside a label changes what it matches, silently; the record's tasks are typically evolved with only 26 of the ~200 table entries enabled (the instruction set is a config file)
organs.human_prior: Ray's Tierra (1991) introduced nop-templates; Avida's three-nop alphabet and register modification are Ofria/Brown/Adami's redesign
organs.source_boundary: the s_n_array / s_f_array tables and ReadLabel

organs.mechanism: h-search reads the nop label that follows it, takes its COMPLEMENT (Rotate by 1 over the three nops: A->B, B->C, C->A) and searches the genome forward from the start for that complement, leaving the FLOW head after the match and the distance in BX; if-label compares the complement of the label just read with the label most recently copied, so a program can detect that it has finished copying its own end marker; a search that finds nothing leaves the head where it was
organs.input: a label read from the genome; the genome
organs.output: a head position; a skip decision
organs.state: the flow head; the read label
assumptions: complement matching means a program never matches its own search template accidentally; the default ancestor uses nop-A nop-B ... nop-C nop-A as the copy-loop markers
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the self-copy loop terminates by recognising its own end label rather than by counting; loops survive length changes
organs.human_prior: Tierra's template addressing; the complement rule is Avida's

organs.human_name: Inst_HeadCopy (7130-7175); the copy-time rates in cMutationRates
organs.mechanism: h-copy reads the instruction under the READ head, and with probability copy_mut_prob replaces it with a random instruction from the set before writing it under the WRITE head (flagging the site); then, each with its own probability, inserts a random instruction, deletes one, applies a uniform mutation, or SLIPS (jumps the read head or duplicates/deletes a stretch); both heads advance; the parent program itself decides when and where to copy
organs.input: the genome under the read head; the mutation rates
organs.output: one instruction written (possibly wrong) under the write head
organs.state: the read and write heads; per-site flags (copied, mutated)
assumptions: mutation is an error in the organism's OWN copying act, so an organism that copies less (or copies fewer sites) exposes itself to fewer errors -- the rate is per copied instruction, not per generation
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: variation is produced by the same machinery selection acts on; slip mutations give whole-block duplications (the source of length change)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: an organism can evolve to skip copying part of itself (checked by the divide gate below)
organs.human_prior: copy-time error as THE mutation source (Tierra); Avida adds divide-time and inject-time classes
organs.source_boundary: Inst_HeadCopy and the copy-time TestCopy* probes

organs.mechanism: a divide instruction succeeds only if: the parent has executed at least JUV_PERIOD and MIN_CYCLES instructions; both halves are within OFFSPRING_SIZE_RANGE of the genome length and within absolute bounds; the parent executed at least MIN_EXE_LINES fraction of its length; the offspring has at least MIN_COPIED_LINES fraction of its sites actually written by h-copy; optionally the offspring must be an exact copy (REQUIRE_EXACT_COPY); then the memory is cropped at the divide point, divide-time mutations are applied, and the parent is reset
organs.input: the parent memory, the divide point, the execution/copy flags
organs.output: an offspring genome or a fault (divide fails, parent continues)
assumptions: a program that divides without copying (or after copying junk) is a cheat the world must refuse, or replication collapses to trivial short genomes
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: closes the shortcut of 'divide immediately'; the fractions are the world's minimum notion of a real copy
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; by reading: the thresholds are constants, so an organism can sit exactly at MIN_COPIED_LINES
organs.human_prior: the size-range and copied-fraction gates are Avida-specific anti-cheat rules (not in Tierra)

organs.mechanism: after a successful divide the offspring genome receives, independently: slip, transposition, lateral-gene-transfer, point, insertion, deletion, uniform mutations, each drawn either per site (binomial over genome length, divided by a mut_multiplier), or at most once per divide, or Poisson with a constant genomic mean; parent mutations (applied to the parent's own memory) exist too; meta-mutation can perturb the copy-mutation rate itself
organs.input: the offspring genome; the rate table
assumptions: divide-time mutation decouples variation from the copy act (a different evolutionary regime from copy-time error, selectable by config)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: experiments can hold the genomic mutation rate constant across genome lengths (the Poisson class) -- a control the copy-time class cannot offer
organs.human_prior: the per-site vs per-genome distinction is the experimenter's, encoded as three rate families

organs.mechanism: merit = base x bonus, where base is a size measure chosen by BASE_MERIT_METHOD (copied size, executed size, full length, least of them, sqrt of least, or a bonus-instruction count) and bonus starts at DEFAULT_BONUS and is modified by reactions during the organism's life; the product is locked in when the organism divides (DivideReset) and the offspring is born with the parent's merit (INHERIT_MERIT) or the bare size merit; fitness (for statistics, not for selection) is merit_base x bonus / gestation_time
organs.input: size counts; the bonus from the environment; gestation time
organs.output: merit (the scheduler's priority); fitness (a reported number)
organs.update: bonus per reaction; merit per divide
assumptions: size in the base term compensates for the fact that a longer genome needs more cycles to copy: without it, the shortest replicator always wins
merit is inherited so a lineage's rewards persist until its offspring earn their own
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one scalar carries both 'how much work is a copy' and 'what has this program computed'; selection acts on the product
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with BASE_MERIT_FULL_SIZE an organism gains merit by growing junk; the LEAST_SIZE options exist because of that
organs.human_prior: merit x bonus, and merit/gestation as fitness, are Avida's central design decisions (Ofria & Wilke 2004)
organs.source_boundary: the merit fields of cPhenotype and their two writers

organs.human_name: cEnvironment::DoProcesses (1610-1760); the reaction process types (170-176); cTaskLib::AddTask (73-142)
organs.mechanism: when an organism's output matches a task on its inputs (the library: echo, add, sub, not, nand, and, orn, or, andn, nor, xor, equ, three-input logic 3AA-3AV, ...), each reaction process computes consumed = min(max, resource available x max_fraction) x task_quality, and bonus = consumed x value; the bonus is applied to the phenotype as ADD, MULT (bonus *= value), POW (bonus *= 2^value), LIN (value x task count), or into energy; resources may be depletable (a finite pool shared by the population) or unlimited (resource NULL: consumed = max x quality)
organs.input: the organism's I/O history; the environment's reaction list; resource levels
assumptions: logic functions on 32-bit inputs are the world's notion of computation; the 'nand' primitive is the only logic instruction, so every other function must be built from it
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the reward structure (multiplicative doubling by task complexity in the classic EQU experiments) is what makes complex functions evolve from simpler ones (Lenski et al. 2003)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with unlimited resources the bonus is a pure function of the genome; with depletable resources it is frequency-dependent
organs.human_prior: the logic-9 environment and its 2^n reward ladder are the experimenter's world design, not the organism's

organs.mechanism: every cell's priority is its organism's merit (times a deme merit if any); the INTEGRATED scheduler decomposes each merit into powers of two and alternates 'the best' with 'everything else' recursively so that time slices are spread as evenly as possible while honouring the ratios; the PROBABILISTIC scheduler draws the next cell with probability proportional to merit; ROUND_ROBIN ignores merit; each schedule step executes ONE instruction of the chosen organism
organs.input: merits; a clock of instruction slots
organs.update: per instruction executed and per merit change
assumptions: CPU cycles are the only currency; an organism's reproductive rate is its merit divided by the cycles a copy costs
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: selection is implemented as scheduling: nothing 'chooses' survivors, higher merit simply runs more often
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the integrated scheduler is deterministic given merits, so identical-merit populations execute in a fixed order (a hidden bias the probabilistic scheduler removes at the cost of variance)
organs.human_prior: merit-proportional time slicing (Adami/Brown 1994) is the ecological law of the world; the binary-decomposition trick is an implementation choice
organs.source_boundary: the scheduler classes and the three cPopulation methods

organs.mechanism: a newborn is assigned a cell by BIRTH_METHOD: a random cell in the whole population (optionally preferring empty cells), the ELDEST cell via a reaper queue, a random cell in the parent's deme, the cell the parent faces, a neighbourhood cell (handlers), or a migration target; population caps kill a random or the oldest organism first; then ActivateOrganism KILLS whatever occupies the target cell and inserts the newborn; death is therefore mostly replacement, not aging
assumptions: space is the second finite resource; a full world means every birth is a death
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the geometry of placement (well-mixed vs neighbourhood) is what makes spatial structure an experimental variable
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: FULL_SOUP_RANDOM with a full world gives every organism the same expected lifetime regardless of merit, so selection acts only through birth rate
organs.human_prior: the birth-method menu is the experimenter's; 'kill the occupant' is Tierra's reaper generalised
organs.source_boundary: PositionOffspring and the KillOrganism call in ActivateOrganism

organs.mechanism: if DEATH_METHOD is on, each organism draws at birth a maximum instruction count = AGE_LIMIT + N(0,1) x AGE_DEVIATION, optionally multiplied by genome length; an organism that executes more than that dies regardless of merit
assumptions: a lifetime cap prevents an immortal non-replicating high-merit organism from holding a cell forever
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the only death that is not replacement; off by default
organs.source_boundary: the DEATH_METHOD block in cOrganism's constructor

organs.human_name: _wait_gen.expo (factor * base ** n, then max_value forever), fibo, constant, runtime (value(ret_or_exc)); _common._init_wait_gen (send(None) to prime)
organs.mechanism: each schedule is a generator that first yields nothing (to absorb the priming send) and then yields waits on demand; expo yields factor * base^n while below the cap and the cap forever after; fibo likewise; constant iterates a value or an iterable; runtime receives the failed call's return value or exception through send() and computes the wait from it (e.g. a Retry-After header); the loop calls wait.send(value) once per failure
organs.input: base, factor, max_value; per failure, the value or exception
organs.state: n (the failure count) inside the generator
assumptions: a generator is the right shape for a stateful schedule that may need the failure's content
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one interface for every schedule, including server-directed ones
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: expo with no cap grows without bound; the cap is the caller's responsibility

organs.human_name: _jitter.full_jitter (random.uniform(0, value)); random_jitter (value + random()) as the pre-1.2 default; _common._next_wait applies it and clamps to the remaining max_time
organs.mechanism: the scheduled wait is replaced by a uniform draw on [0, wait] (full jitter, the AWS 2015 analysis: lowest total work and contention among the jitter variants) or, in the older scheme, increased by up to one second; the result is then clamped so the sleep never exceeds the remaining wall-clock budget
assumptions: many clients retrying the same failure synchronise their retries unless the waits are randomised; spreading over the whole interval beats adding a small offset
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: thundering-herd avoidance; expected wait halves relative to the schedule
organs.human_prior: Brooker, AWS Architecture Blog 2015 'Exponential Backoff And Jitter'

organs.human_name: _sync.retry_exception / retry_predicate (1-132): tries, elapsed, giveup(e), max_tries, max_time, StopIteration from the schedule, on_success / on_backoff / on_giveup handlers, raise_on_giveup
organs.mechanism: call the target; on the named exception (or a predicate on the return value) decide: give up if the give-up predicate says so, the try count is reached, or the elapsed time exceeds the budget (then call the give-up handlers and re-raise or return None); otherwise ask the schedule for the next wait (a schedule that is exhausted also gives up), call the backoff handlers with the details, sleep, retry; success calls its handlers and returns
organs.output: the result, or a raised exception after giving up
assumptions: failures are transient with some probability; the caller can classify permanent ones (giveup) so they are not retried
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: retry policy separated from the call site as a decorator
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: max_tries counts attempts, so max_tries = 1 means no retry; the elapsed check happens before the sleep, so the final sleep is clamped by _next_wait rather than skipped

organs.human_name: hammurabi.bas: 310 (land price 17-26), 800 (C = RND*5+1 yield / rats / babies), 515-533 (harvest, rats when C even: E = S/C, immigrants), 540-555 (fed = Q/20; starved D; impeach if D > 0.45 P), 542 (plague: Q < 0 with probability 0.15), 860-896 (final grading by starvation percent and acres per person)
organs.mechanism: each year: report; halve the population on a plague (15 percent); price land at 17-26 per acre (uniform); take buy/sell, feed and plant decisions, each validated against stock, acreage and one tender per ten acres; draw one uniform 1-5 that serves as the yield per acre, then redraw: if the draw is even, rats eat stock/C; immigration = C * (20 A + S) / P / 100 + 1; people fed = Q/20; if more than 45 percent starve the game ends with impeachment; after ten years grade on average starvation percent and acres per person
organs.state: P, S, A, Y, and the two running tallies
assumptions: one uniform draw reused for yield, rats and immigration is enough randomness for a game; the grade thresholds (3, 10, 33 percent; 7, 9, 10 acres) define what good governance means
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the most copied 'resource management under uncertainty' toy of the era; every constant is visible
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the same draw C drives yield and immigration, so a bad harvest also means few immigrants (a correlation the player cannot see); plague is independent of everything

organs.human_name: superstartrek.bas: 370 (E = 3000, Klingons and stardates random), 475 (FNR), 2880-3000 (damage: a random device D(R1) gains or loses a random amount), 4250-4550 (phasers: X units split over Klingons, hit H = (X/K3 / distance) * (RND + 2), a hit below 15 percent of the target's energy is absorbed)
organs.mechanism: one energy pool pays for warp movement, shields and phaser fire; a phaser volley of X units is divided among the Klingons in the quadrant and scaled by inverse distance and a random factor in [2, 3); a hit smaller than 15 percent of the target's remaining energy does no damage; after actions, with probability 0.2 a random subsystem is damaged or repaired by a random amount, disabling the corresponding command until repaired; Klingons return fire when the ship moves
assumptions: a single budget makes every choice a trade-off; random subsystem damage forces plan changes
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the most copied game of the 1970s (the record); a budget-and-risk loop in 425 lines
organs.source_boundary: superstartrek.bas; CANDIDATE because read by grep, not line by line

organs.human_name: GC_mark_from (518-640): mse_start / mse_descr; GC_DS_LENGTH (split at 128 words), GC_DS_BITMAP (one bit per word says 'may be a pointer'), GC_DS_PROC; credit = HBLKSIZE
organs.mechanism: the mark stack holds (start, descriptor) entries; a descriptor is a length (scan every word), a bitmap (scan flagged words: the 'typed' allocation hook), or a procedure; long ranges are split so the stack does not explode (and, under PARALLEL_MARK, halved for stealing); each candidate word is range-checked against the least/greatest plausible heap address, prefetched, then pushed via the header lookup; the loop runs until the stack is empty or a byte credit is spent, so marking can be resumed (the incremental hook)
organs.output: mark bits set in block headers
organs.state: the mark stack (grown on overflow, GC_signal_mark_stack_overflow)
assumptions: a fast range test rejects most non-pointers before the header lookup; splitting ranges bounds stack depth independently of object size
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: marking cost is per candidate word with a cheap first filter; the same loop serves precise (bitmap) and conservative (length) objects
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: everything that looks like a pointer is retained (the conservative premise); large integer-heavy objects (GC_DS_LENGTH) are scanned in full unless allocated atomic
organs.human_prior: Boehm & Weiser 1988 'Garbage collection in an uncooperative environment'

organs.human_name: headers.c GC_find_header / GC_header_cache_miss / get_index (28-262): GC_top_index[hi] -> bottom_index -> hdr; IS_FORWARDING_ADDR_OR_NIL; GC_all_interior_pointers -> GC_base; mark.c GC_mark_and_push (1343-1360) with HBLK_IS_FREE and the black-list add
organs.mechanism: the address space is indexed in two levels (a top array by high bits, optionally hashed, and per-top-entry bottom arrays of per-block header pointers); a candidate word's block is looked up; a nil or forwarding entry means not a heap object (or, for large objects spanning blocks, the forwarding count walks back to the first block); if interior pointers are allowed, GC_base finds the object start; a free block or no header means the word was not a pointer, and the (page, source) pair is added to a black list; otherwise the object's mark bit is set and it is pushed; a small header cache fronts the index
organs.output: an object to mark, or nothing
organs.state: the index; the header cache; the black lists
assumptions: block headers are allocated out of line so a stray write cannot corrupt them; the index answers 'is this a heap pointer' in O(1) for any word, which is what makes conservatism affordable
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no cooperation from the compiler or the program: any C object can be collected
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: false retention is the known cost, bounded by the black lists and by the allocator avoiding black-listed pages for large objects (the comment: false hits from the stack 'can pin a large object that spans the block')
organs.human_prior: the 1988 paper's 'page table' plus Boehm's later black-listing (1993 'Space efficient conservative garbage collection')
organs.source_boundary: headers.c + the push functions + blacklst.c's interface

organs.human_name: alloc.c min_bytes_allocd (309-350): scan_size = 2 composite + atomic/4 + 2 stack + roots; result = scan_size / GC_free_space_divisor (halved if incremental); GC_should_collect (430-456); GC_expand_hp_inner (1562-1628): expansion_slop, GC_collect_at_heapsize, the plausible-address bounds
organs.mechanism: a collection is due when the adjusted bytes allocated since the last GC reach an estimate of the marking work (composite bytes counted twice, atomic bytes a quarter, stacks twice, roots once) divided by the free-space divisor (default 3), or when the heap reaches a size set at the last expansion; expanding the heap adds a slop (the same estimate plus a constant) to the plausible-address bounds so black-listing keeps working, and schedules the next forced collection just before the slop would be consumed; a maximum heap size can refuse expansion
organs.output: collect now / not yet; grow / refuse
organs.update: per allocation that finds no free object
assumptions: the cost of a GC is proportional to what must be scanned, so amortising it against allocation keeps GC time a bounded fraction of mutator time (the divisor is that fraction's knob)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no explicit GC calls; the heap grows only when collection did not free enough
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a program whose live set grows steadily collects more and more often before each expansion (the 'GC before growing' policy); GC_free_space_divisor trades space for time explicitly
organs.human_prior: the standard allocation-triggered policy; the scan-work weighting is Boehm's

organs.human_name: reclaim.c GC_reclaim_clear (180-212): walk a block by sz, unmarked objects linked onto the free list and cleared; allchblk.c GC_freehblk (934-993): merge with successor and predecessor free blocks
organs.mechanism: small objects live in blocks of a single size class; after marking, a block is swept only when its size class's free list is empty (lazy), by walking the block and threading every unmarked object onto the list (optionally clearing it); a block with no marks is returned whole; large blocks are freed into a free list keyed by size and merged with a free successor (by address) and a free predecessor (found via the header index), with the merged header removed
organs.state: the free lists per size class; the large-block lists
organs.update: per allocation miss / per large free
assumptions: sweeping on demand spreads the cost across allocations; size-segregated blocks make the sweep a stride walk
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no sweep pause; allocation from a free list is a pop

organs.human_name: btb_pc_q / btb_target_q / btb_is_*_q; the two lookup loops; btb_hit_r / btb_miss_r; u_lru (biriscv_npc_lfsr)
organs.mechanism: 32 entries each holding a branch PC, its last target and three type bits; the lookup compares every entry against the fetch PC (and, for a 64-bit fetch, against PC | 4 for the upper slot); on a resolved branch a hit updates the target (if taken) and type bits in place, a miss allocates an entry chosen by an LFSR (pseudo-random replacement, not LRU despite the instance name)
organs.output: btb_valid, target, type bits, upper-slot flag
assumptions: a branch's target is usually the same next time (true for direct branches, false for indirect ones)
32 entries cover the hot loops
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the target is known at fetch, one cycle before decode; without it a taken branch costs the pipeline depth
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: fully associative compare of 32 entries every cycle is the timing-critical path; random replacement can evict a hot loop's branch
organs.human_prior: the BTB (Lee & Smith 1984); random replacement is the designer's area/timing choice
organs.source_boundary: the BTB registers, the two always @* lookup loops, the write block

organs.mechanism: 512 two-bit counters initialised to 3 (strongly taken); a resolved taken branch increments its counter (saturating at 3), not-taken decrements (at 0); predict taken when the counter >= 2; the index is either PC bits (bimodal) or, with GSHARE_ENABLE, PC bits XOR the global history register; the read uses the SPECULATIVE history, the write uses the ARCHITECTURAL one at resolve time
organs.input: the fetch PC; the history; resolve events
assumptions: a branch's recent behaviour predicts its next outcome (bimodal) or its behaviour correlated with recent global outcomes does (gshare)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: hysteresis: one anomalous outcome does not flip the prediction; gshare captures correlated branches at the cost of aliasing
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: 512 entries alias heavily in large code; GSHARE is OFF by default in the parameter list, so the shipped configuration is bimodal

organs.mechanism: an 8-entry circular stack of return addresses; on a PREDICTED call (BTB says call) the fetch PC + 4 is pushed and the speculative pointer advanced; a predicted return pops it and supplies the target; on a RESOLVED call/return the architectural pointer moves and, for a call, the real return address is written; a resolved branch resets the speculative pointer from the architectural one, discarding the speculative pushes/pops of a mispredicted path; an entry equal to RAS_INVALID (bit 0 set) disables the prediction
organs.input: BTB type bits at fetch; resolve events
organs.output: the predicted return PC; a valid flag
organs.update: per predicted and per resolved call/return
assumptions: calls and returns nest (a stack); 8 deep covers the hot call depth
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: indirect returns, which the BTB cannot predict after a call from a new site, become predictable
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: overflow wraps silently (deep recursion mispredicts every return beyond 8); the invalid marker is bit 0 of the stored address, which relies on aligned return addresses
organs.human_prior: the RAS (Kaeli & Emma 1991); the dual-pointer recovery scheme is the designer's
organs.source_boundary: the RAS registers and the four always blocks that touch them

organs.human_name: global_history_q vs global_history_real_q; ras_index_q vs ras_index_real_q
organs.mechanism: two copies of the global history: the real one shifts in each RESOLVED outcome; the speculative one shifts in each PREDICTION as it is made (so back-to-back predictions see the effect of earlier predictions) and, on any resolve, is reloaded from the real one plus the resolved outcome; the RAS pointer follows the same pattern
assumptions: predictions are usually right, so the speculative copy is usually the truth one step early; when wrong, resynchronisation costs nothing beyond the pipeline flush that already happens
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: prediction can proceed at fetch rate without waiting for resolution; the classic speculative-update problem solved by shadowing

organs.mechanism: next PC = the RAS top if the BTB says this is a return (and the entry is valid); else the BTB target if the BHT predicts taken or the BTB says unconditional jump; else the fall-through (PC aligned to 8 plus 8, i.e. the next 64-bit fetch pair); next_taken flags which of the two 32-bit slots redirects, so the decode stage can drop the instruction after a taken branch in the pair

organs.mechanism: at most one segment is timed at a time: when a new segment is sent and nothing is being timed, t_rtt=1 and t_rtseq = its first sequence number; the slow timer increments t_rtt every 500 ms; when an ACK covers t_rtseq the sample t_rtt is folded in as srtt = alpha*srtt + (1-alpha)*rtt with alpha=0.9 (first sample sets srtt directly); the sample is in 500 ms ticks

assumptions: a retransmitted segment is never timed (the timer is started only on new data; but a sample taken across a retransmission is NOT excluded here: t_rtt keeps counting through a REXMT and the ACK for the retransmitted data still satisfies SEQ_GT(ack, t_rtseq)) -- the Karn problem is present by reading
500 ms resolution; the first sample is trusted fully

organs.failure_landscape: by reading: no variance term, so a bursty path produces spurious timeouts at beta=2; ambiguous samples after retransmission bias srtt low; no measurement

organs.mechanism: on sending with no timer running: REXMT = clamp(beta*srtt, 1 s, 30 s), shift=0; on expiry: shift++, if shift > 10 drop the connection (ETIMEDOUT); else REXMT = clamp(srtt * backoff[shift-1]) with backoff = {1.0,1.2,1.4,1.7,2.0,3.0,5.0,8.0,16.0,32.0} (or srtt << shift when the tcpexprexmtbackoff switch is on -- a compiled-in alternative, off by default); then snd_nxt = snd_una and ONE segment is (re)sent ('this only transmits one segment!'); an ACK that advances snd_una resets shift to 0 and the timer to beta*srtt
organs.output: a retransmission of the oldest unacked segment; the next timeout; or a dropped connection
organs.update: on send, on ACK, on expiry
assumptions: a timeout means the segment was lost, not that the network is full (the record's failure: this is where 4.3 Tahoe reads congestion)
the backoff table is gentle at first (1.0, 1.2, 1.4) -- the first three retransmissions come at nearly the same interval
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: reliability: nothing unacknowledged is ever abandoned short of ten timeouts
organs.failure_landscape: the record's: under shared-link congestion every host's timer fires, every host resends into the queue, throughput collapses three orders of magnitude; the gentle table makes it worse than pure doubling
organs.human_prior: the ten-entry table vs the exponential switch: two policies, one compiled in, one chosen at runtime by a global; the table is the default
organs.source_boundary: case TCPT_REXMT and the two timer-set sites

organs.human_name: tcp_output.c 51-57: len = MIN(sb_cc, snd_wnd + t_force) - off
organs.mechanism: the amount eligible to send is whatever is in the socket buffer up to the peer's advertised window (snd_wnd, updated from segments that pass the wl1/wl2 freshness test, tcp_input.c 578-586), minus what is already in flight; capped per segment at t_maxseg (negotiated at SYN as min(rcv_hiwat/2, 1024)); 'sendalot' loops until the window or buffer is exhausted. No sender-side variable other than snd_wnd limits in-flight data
organs.output: len for this segment; whether to loop
organs.update: per output call; snd_wnd per fresh window advertisement
assumptions: the receiver's buffer is the only scarce resource worth modelling; the path between the hosts is not modelled at all
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: flow control: the receiver is never overrun
organs.failure_landscape: a full window is dumped into the network at once at connection start and after every timeout (no slow start); with many senders on one link the shared queue overflows -- the 1986 collapse
organs.human_prior: RFC 793 window semantics implemented literally; the absence of a network model is the era's prior

organs.mechanism: the advertised window is the free receive-buffer space, but advertised as 0 if below a quarter of the buffer (receiver silly window avoidance); a segment is sent solely to update the window when the newly available space is >= 35% of the buffer; rcv_adv remembers the largest edge advertised
assumptions: window updates are unreliable (no ACK for an ACK), so the peer's persist timer covers the loss (the comment block at tcp_output.c 99-116)

organs.mechanism: four short counters per connection (REXMT, PERSIST, KEEP, 2MSL); a global 500 ms routine walks every control block, decrements every nonzero counter and dispatches the expiry to tcp_timers via the user-request switch; all timer values are clamped by TCPT_RANGESET to [min,max] in ticks; the same sweep ages t_idle and t_rtt and advances the initial sequence number

organs.human_name: tcp_input.c 885-900 (cw > ssthresh ? incr = mss^2/cw + mss/8 : incr = mss); tcp_output.c 89 (win = min(snd_wnd, snd_cwnd)); tcp_timer.c 222-229 (reset on timeout)
organs.mechanism: the sender's usable window is the minimum of the receiver's advertisement and a local snd_cwnd; each new ACK adds one segment to cwnd while cwnd < ssthresh (doubling per round trip), and mss^2/cwnd plus mss/8 above it (about one segment per round trip); on a retransmit timeout ssthresh becomes half the window in flight (at least two segments) and cwnd becomes one segment, restarting the exponential phase
assumptions: packet loss signals congestion; the network's capacity is discovered by probing upward and backing off multiplicatively on loss (the AIMD premise)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the 1986 congestion collapse ended; the sender no longer dumps a full window after a loss
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: loss is the only signal, so the window oscillates around the bottleneck (the sawtooth); the mss/8 term ('to help larger windows open quickly enough') is a tuning constant without derivation
organs.human_prior: Jacobson 1988 'Congestion Avoidance and Control' (the Tahoe algorithms); this file is the Reno release of them
organs.source_boundary: the cwnd arithmetic in the three files

organs.human_name: tcp_input.c 790-855: t_dupacks, tcprexmtthresh = 3, the 'Kludge snd_nxt & the congestion window so we send only this one packet' block, the inflate branch, and the deflate on the next new ACK
organs.mechanism: a pure duplicate ACK (no data, unchanged window, ack == snd_una, retransmit timer running) increments t_dupacks; at exactly three: ssthresh = half the flight (min 2 segments), snd_nxt is pulled back to the acked point, cwnd is set to ONE segment so tcp_output sends exactly the missing segment, then cwnd is set to ssthresh + 3 segments and snd_nxt restored; each further duplicate adds one segment to cwnd and calls tcp_output (new data flows as duplicates confirm departures); the first ACK that advances snd_una deflates cwnd back to ssthresh and zeroes the counter; any non-duplicate resets the counter
organs.output: one retransmission; a temporarily inflated window
assumptions: three duplicates mean a loss rather than reordering (tcprexmtthresh is a global tunable); each duplicate ACK proves one packet left the network, so the window may grow by one without adding load ('packet conservation')
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a single loss no longer costs a timeout and a slow-start from one segment; throughput on lightly lossy paths roughly doubled (Fall & Floyd 1996 measured the lineage)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the mechanism assumes one loss per window; two losses in a window leave the second to the timer (the NewReno / SACK problem, not addressed in this body); the deflate to ssthresh on the first new ACK is the 'Reno' step Tahoe lacked
organs.human_prior: Jacobson's 1990 fast recovery (email to end2end-interest); fast retransmit is Tahoe's
organs.source_boundary: the duplicate-ACK block and the deflate lines

organs.mechanism: if the connection is established, the segment has only ACK set, is in sequence, carries the same window and nothing is being retransmitted, then: a zero-length segment whose ACK advances (and cwnd >= snd_wnd, i.e. not in slow start) is handled as a pure ACK (drop acked data, update RTT, restart or stop the timer, wake the writer) and returns; a data segment at the expected ack with an empty reassembly queue and buffer space is appended and a delayed ACK noted; everything else falls through to the full input processing
assumptions: bulk transfer in one direction is the common case; the checks are cheaper than the general path
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: per-packet processing cost cut for the common case (Van Jacobson's 'header prediction')
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the fast path bypasses the cwnd opening, which is why it is guarded by cwnd >= snd_wnd (only when cwnd is no longer the constraint)

organs.human_name: tcp_input.c 768-826: delta = t_rtt - 1 - (t_srtt >> 3); t_srtt += delta; delta = |delta| - (t_rttvar >> 2); t_rttvar += delta; first sample: srtt = rtt << 3, rttvar = rtt << 1; t_rxtshift = 0 on a measured sample; RTO = ((srtt >> 2) + rttvar) >> 1 bounded by TCPTV_MIN / REXMTMAX; the comment 'This replaces rfc793's wired-in beta'
organs.mechanism: each measured round trip updates the smoothed RTT by one eighth of the error (srtt kept scaled by 8 so the update is an integer shift) and a smoothed mean deviation by one quarter of the absolute error (scaled by 4); the retransmit timeout is srtt + 2 rttvar; a sample is taken only for a segment that was not retransmitted (the timer is not restarted on retransmission) and a measured sample resets the exponential backoff shift, which is Karn's algorithm; the first sample seeds the deviation at half the RTT so the first timeout is 2 RTT
organs.input: one timed segment at a time
assumptions: a fixed multiplier (4.2's beta = 2) under-estimates the timeout on variable paths and over-estimates it on stable ones; a variance term tracks the path's variability; integer shifts are cheap on 1988 hardware
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the spurious retransmissions that fed the 1986 collapse stop; the estimator every TCP still uses (RFC 6298)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the mean deviation under-estimates the standard deviation (Jacobson chose it for cost); the sample granularity is the 500 ms tick, so RTTs below it are all 'one tick'

organs.human_name: tcp_input.c 835-852: incr = mss; if cwnd > ssthresh then incr = max(mss^2 / cwnd, 1); cwnd = min(cwnd + incr, IP_MAXPACKET); tcp_timer.c 216-223: on REXMT, ssthresh = max(2, min(wnd, cwnd) / 2 / mss) * mss, cwnd = mss

assumptions: packet loss means congestion; the network's capacity is found by exponential probing and held by linear probing (the AIMD argument of Jacobson 1988 and Chiu & Jain 1989)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the end of congestion collapse on the 1986-88 ARPANET; this file is the origin of the mechanism
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: after any loss the window restarts from one segment (slow start), so a single loss on a long path costs the whole pipe (Reno's motivation)

organs.human_name: tcp_input.c 720-760: t_dupacks; tcprexmtthresh 3; on the third: ssthresh = half the window, snd_nxt = ack, cwnd = mss, tcp_output, snd_nxt restored; the comment 'Leave here with the congestion window set to allow 2 packets on the next real ack'; NO cwnd inflation branch, NO deflate on the next new ACK

organs.output: one early retransmission and a slow-start restart
assumptions: three duplicates mean a loss, not reordering; the pipe is allowed to drain (the cost Reno removed)

organs.human_prior: Jacobson's fast retransmit (1988 revision); fast recovery is the 1990 Reno addition

organs.human_name: buddy_tree_mark / buddy_tree_release / update_parent_chain (1761-1813); the node encoding (internal_position: local_offset = bits per node at that depth)
organs.mechanism: each tree node holds a number: 0 for fully free at its own size, its depth-relative maximum for fully used, otherwise the largest free block order below it; marking a node writes its max value, releasing writes 0; either then walks to the root: parent = (either child nonzero) * (min(children) + 1); the walk returns early the first time a parent already holds that value, so most updates touch O(1) nodes
organs.state: the bitset (ceil(log2 size) levels of nodes, node width growing by one bit per level toward the root)
assumptions: a node's summary (largest free order below) is enough to route an allocation without visiting the leaves; the early stop is sound because a parent's value depends only on its two children
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: alloc and free are O(depth) with a memory overhead of a few bits per block rather than a free list per order
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: an allocation of a size much smaller than the alignment still costs the full descent; coalescing is implicit (a parent reads 0 when both children read 0), so there is no explicit buddy-merge step to get wrong
organs.human_prior: Knowlton 1965 / Knuth's buddy system, usually implemented with per-order free lists; the packed-tree encoding is this author's

organs.mechanism: starting at the root with target_status = depth-1, refuse if the root's summary exceeds the target; at each level compare the left child's value against the target: if the left cannot fit go right, if the right cannot fit go left, else read the right child's value and go left when left is equal or more busy than right (prefer the busier side), or left when right is completely empty; the descent ends at the target depth without a search
assumptions: packing new allocations into already-fragmented subtrees preserves fully-free subtrees for large requests (a best-fit heuristic by summary value)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: O(depth) allocation with a fragmentation-avoiding choice at every level for free
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; the README claims low fragmentation, not measured here

organs.mechanism: the tree is sized for the next power of two above the arena; the difference (delta) is masked by walking down the right spine, marking whole right children whenever delta exceeds half the node, until delta is exactly one node; resizing unmarks them the same way; allocation then never sees the phantom space
organs.output: a tree with the tail marked
assumptions: a power-of-two tree plus a used-marked tail is simpler than a tree of arbitrary shape
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: arbitrary arena sizes with the unchanged power-of-two machinery

organs.human_name: bdd_makenode (kernel.c 1258-1330): low == high -> low; NODEHASH chain walk; free-list pop; on exhaustion bdd_gbc, then reorder via longjmp if node usage crossed usednodes_nextreorder, then resize if free nodes fall below minfreenodes percent
organs.mechanism: a node request (level, low, high) first returns low if the children are equal (the reduction rule), then walks the hash chain for an existing node with the same triple and returns its index; otherwise a node is taken from the free list; if none is free, garbage collect; if the collection reveals the node count has crossed the reorder trigger and reordering is enabled, abandon the current operation by longjmp to the operator entry (which restarts it after reordering); if free nodes are still scarce, grow the table and rehash
organs.state: the node array with hash chains and refcounts; the free list
assumptions: hash-consing every node makes equality of functions equality of integers (the ROBDD canonicity theorem, Bryant 1986); the free/gc/resize/reorder ladder keeps the invariant under memory pressure
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: satisfiability, equivalence and counting become O(1) or linear in the DAG; the table is the whole representation
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the longjmp restart of an operation mid-recursion is the cost of reordering from inside makenode; the panic path returns 0 (false) with an error code when nothing can be freed
organs.human_prior: Bryant 1986; the unique table with a free list and gc is Brace, Rudell, Bryant 1990 (the CUDD lineage)
organs.source_boundary: bdd_makenode and the gc/resize hooks it calls

organs.human_name: cmaes_SamplePopulation (608-658): x = m + sigma B (D z); cmaes_UpdateEigensystem (1881-1930): skip if up to date, if gen < last + modulo, or if eigen time exceeds 20 percent of total; the diagonal-only phase (diagonalCov iterations)
organs.mechanism: for each of lambda offspring draw z ~ N(0, I), scale by the eigenvalue square roots D, rotate by the eigenvectors B, scale by sigma and add the mean; the decomposition is recomputed only when flagged stale AND (a generation modulo has elapsed, default 1/(10 ccov N), OR when the eigen time is below 20 percent of the run's time); for the first diagonalCov generations (default 2 + 100 N / sqrt(lambda)) C is treated as diagonal and no decomposition happens; TestMinStdDevs inflates sigma until every coordinate's std exceeds a floor
assumptions: the O(N^3) decomposition can lag the O(N^2) covariance update by several generations without hurting progress; a diagonal start is cheaper and good enough early
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the per-generation cost is O(N^2 lambda) except when the decomposition runs; the time cap makes the algorithm's overhead a bounded fraction
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a stale decomposition samples from an outdated shape; the 20 percent rule is a wall-clock heuristic, so results differ between machines when it triggers
organs.human_prior: Hansen & Ostermeier 2001; the lazy update is the implementation's

organs.human_name: cmaes_UpdateDistribution (860-905): rgBDz = sqrt(mueff) (m_new - m_old)/sigma; rgdTmp = D^-1 B' rgBDz; ps = (1-cs) ps + sqrt(cs(2-cs)) B rgdTmp; hsig = ||ps|| / sqrt(1-(1-cs)^(2 gen)) / chiN < 1.4 + 2/(N+1); pc = (1-cc) pc + hsig sqrt(cc(2-cc)) rgBDz
organs.mechanism: the selected mean shift, scaled by sqrt(mu_eff)/sigma, is the per-generation evidence; the step-size path ps accumulates it after whitening (B D^-1 B') so that under random selection it is a standard normal vector of expected length chiN; the covariance path pc accumulates it unwhitened; hsig compares the normalised length of ps against a threshold and, when the path is too long (the mean is moving fast, typically early or after a jump), zeroes pc's update so the covariance does not learn a spurious direction; the initial-phase flag ends when ps's length statistic settles
assumptions: consecutive selected steps that point the same way are signal (the path grows); steps that cancel are noise (the path stays short); the whitened path's length under no selection is known, so it is a calibrated test statistic
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: step-size control without a success-rate rule; the covariance learns from correlations across generations, not only within one
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the threshold constants (1.4 + 2/(N+1)) are tuned; the sqrt(1-(1-cs)^(2 gen)) bias correction matters only early; the flat-fitness escape multiplies sigma by exp(0.2 + cs/damps) with a warning
organs.human_prior: Hansen & Ostermeier 1996/2001 (cumulative step-size adaptation); Hansen 2016 tutorial for hsig

organs.human_name: Adapt_C2 (927-965): C = (1 - c1 - cmu) C + c1 (pc pc' + (1-hsig) cc(2-cc) C) + cmu sum_k w_k y_k y_k'; SupplementDefaults: lambda = 4 + 3 ln N, mu = lambda/2, cs = (mueff+2)/(N+mueff+3), cc = 4/(N+4), ccov from 2/(N+1.414)^2 and (2 mueff - 1)/((N+2)^2 + mueff), damps = 1 + 2 max(0, sqrt((mueff-1)/(N+1)) - 1) + cs
organs.mechanism: the lower triangle of C is blended: decayed by (1 - c1 - cmu), plus the outer product of the covariance path (with a variance-loss correction when hsig was zero), plus the weighted outer products of the mu selected steps (y_k = (x_k - m_old)/sigma); learning rates split a total ccov between the rank-one and rank-mu parts by 1/mucov; the decomposition is flagged stale; min/max diagonal are tracked for the termination tests; all constants come from formulas in N, mu_eff and lambda unless a parameter file overrides them
assumptions: the selected steps' second moment, accumulated with a slow learning rate, estimates a covariance under which the successful steps become isotropic (the CMA principle); the defaults are the ones the literature validated
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: invariance under rotations and rescaling of the problem; ill-conditioned problems solved without derivative information
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: O(N^2) memory and O(N^3) decomposition bound N to a few hundred; the flat-fitness and TolUpX warnings are the implementation's own failure detectors

organs.mechanism: sigma grows when the whitened path is longer than a random walk's expected length chiN (selected steps are correlated: the step is too small) and shrinks when shorter (steps cancel: too large); the exponent is scaled by cs/damps, damps defaulting to about 1 + cs for large N
assumptions: path length is a scale-free, rotation-invariant signal of step-size adequacy
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: log-linear convergence on the sphere at a rate independent of the initial sigma

organs.mechanism: two actions at a layer are mutex if one deletes a precondition or effect of the other (interference) or if their preconditions are mutex (competing needs); two facts at a layer are mutex if every pair of their achievers is mutex; the relation is a per-layer bit vector (bvec_len) read by are_mutex; during extraction, choosing an action marks every action mutex with it as unavailable (mark_exclusive) and unmarks on backtrack
organs.input: the layer's actions and their precondition/effect/delete lists

organs.human_name: basicplan (planner.c 191-330): goals_at[time][cindex]; in_edges loop with IS_MARKED skip; goals_still_possible; used / is_true counters; the undo block; action_set_is_minimal at the layer boundary
organs.mechanism: at a layer, take the next unsatisfied goal (skipping goals already made true by chosen actions), try each achiever (no-ops first) that is not marked mutex with a prior choice: mark its exclusions, check every remaining goal still has an unmarked achiever, add its preconditions to the previous layer's goal set (counting uses so duplicates are shared), recurse to the next goal; when all goals at the layer are served, recurse to the previous layer with the new goal set; undo counters and marks on return; success at time 0
organs.input: a goal set at the last layer
organs.output: a plan (the used actions per layer) or failure

organs.mechanism: every ProbeInterval (scaled by awareness) pick the next node of a shuffled ring; send a UDP ping with a sequence number and wait ProbeTimeout for the ack; on timeout ask IndirectChecks (3) random other members to ping it on our behalf (they reply ack or nack), and also try a TCP ping; if nothing comes back within the interval, broadcast a suspect message for the node's current incarnation
organs.state: the probe index / shuffled order, pending ack channels keyed by seqno
assumptions: UDP loss is common and independent; an indirect path distinguishes 'it is dead' from 'my link is bad'
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: constant per-node load regardless of cluster size (SWIM's claim); the record's oracle asserts the suspect -> dead transitions

organs.mechanism: an integer score in [0, max): a probe that got a direct ack subtracts 1, a nack from an indirect helper adds 1, a full miss adds more; ScaleTimeout multiplies ProbeInterval / ProbeTimeout by (score + 1), so a node whose own probes keep failing slows itself down instead of declaring others dead
assumptions: my failures are more likely my fault than everyone else's
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: Lifeguard's fix for false positives from a slow/overloaded prober

organs.mechanism: a suspected node gets a timer between min and max: timeout = max - (log(n + 1) / log(k + 1)) * (max - min), where n is the number of DISTINCT members that have also reported it suspect and k the expected number; each new confirmer (Confirm dedups by name) re-evaluates the remaining time; at expiry the node is declared dead; min = SuspicionMult * log10(cluster size) * ProbeInterval
organs.output: a dead declaration at the timer's end
organs.state: n, the confirmations set, start time
assumptions: independent confirmations are evidence; one suspicious reporter is not
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: Lifeguard's second fix: fewer false positives at the cost of slower detection when only one node notices

organs.mechanism: every membership message carries the subject's incarnation; a node that hears itself suspected (or dead) increments its own incarnation and broadcasts alive with the new number, which supersedes the suspicion; older-incarnation messages are ignored; conflicting alive messages for the same name from different addresses are refused (conflict delegate)
assumptions: UNKNOWN
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: UNKNOWN

organs.human_name: rls_forgetting.m: k = P phi' / (lambda + phi P phi'); P = (P - k phi P) / lambda; theta = theta + k (y - phi theta); main_code.m: phi = [-y(t), -y(t-1), u(t), u(t-1)], lambda = 0.8, P0 = diag(100, 100, 1, 1), theta0 = [0, 0, 0.01, 0.2]
organs.mechanism: the plant is modelled as y(t+1) = -a1 y(t) - a2 y(t-1) + b0 u(t) + b1 u(t-1); each sample forms the regressor from the last two outputs and inputs, computes the gain from the covariance, corrects the parameter estimate by the prediction error, and shrinks the covariance with a forgetting factor of 0.8 so old data is discounted geometrically; the initial covariance is large on the a's and small on the b's, and b0 starts at 0.01 rather than 0 so the first division in the design is finite
assumptions: the plant is linear, second order and slowly varying (forgetting makes the estimator track drift at the price of noise sensitivity); the regressor is persistently excited (the square-wave reference supplies it)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: O(n^2) per step, no matrix inversion; the estimator the textbook builds every adaptive scheme on
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with lambda = 0.8 and no excitation the covariance grows without bound (estimator wind-up), which the script avoids only because the reference keeps switching; b0 near zero makes the design explode
organs.human_prior: Astrom & Wittenmark 1989/1995 Adaptive Control, chapter 2 (RLS with forgetting)

organs.human_name: main_code.m experiment 1 (28-33): r1 = b1/b0, s0 = (am1 - a1)/b0, s1 = (am2 - a2)/b0, t0 = bm0/b0 (zero cancelled); experiment 2 (125-140): r1, s0, s1 from the Diophantine identity with the observer pole a0 and t0 = (1 + am1 + am2)/(b0 + b1), a0 re-estimated as (a2 r1 + b1 s1)/am2; the control law u(t+1) = -r1 u(t) + t0 uc(t) [+ t1 uc(t-1)] - s0 y(t) - s1 y(t-1); reference model am1 = -1.3205, am2 = 0.4966, bm0 = 0.1761
organs.mechanism: with the estimated plant (A, B) and a desired closed-loop denominator Am (from the reference model), solve for R, S such that A R + B S = Am (times an observer polynomial) and set T so the closed loop's DC gain matches the model; variant 1 cancels the plant zero by dividing by b0 (a one-line design that requires the zero to be stable); variant 2 keeps the zero, adds an observer pole a0 and solves the 2x2 identity in closed form; the estimated a0 is updated from the previous solution; the design runs at every sample from the current estimates (certainty equivalence)
assumptions: the estimates are the truth (certainty equivalence); the reference model's poles are achievable; in variant 1 the plant zero is inside the unit circle

organs.mechanism: for every one of 2^(N-M) messages, encode it, multiply the per-bit likelihoods of the resulting codeword, keep the best (block MAP) and accumulate per-bit marginals (bit MAP); refuses more than 31 message bits ('absurd')

assumptions: exact but exponential; exists to calibrate the iterative decoder
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a ground truth inside the body: the instrument ships its own oracle

organs.mechanism: each nonzero of the parity-check matrix H carries two messages (pr: bit-to-check probability ratio; lr: check-to-bit likelihood ratio); initprp sets pr from the channel; each iteration: for every check row, a forward pass accumulates the product of (2/(1+pr) - 1) = (1-p)/(1+p) terms and a backward pass forms each edge's outgoing lr = (1-t)/(1+t) from the product of all OTHER edges (forward x backward partial products, no division); for every bit column the same forward/backward trick multiplies the incoming lr into the channel ratio to produce each edge's outgoing pr and the posterior; the tentative decoding is the sign of the posterior; the loop stops when the tentative word satisfies all checks (or after max_iter; a negative max_iter forces the count)
organs.output: a decoded word, its parity checks, bit posteriors, the iteration count
organs.state: two doubles per nonzero of H
assumptions: the graph is sparse and nearly cycle-free so the product rule is nearly exact (the whole point of LOW density)
a NaN posterior is treated as 1 (a numerical guard, not a theorem)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: near-Shannon-limit decoding in linear time per iteration; the forward/backward partial products make each sweep linear in the nonzeros
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: short cycles in H make the messages overconfident; the decoder can converge to a wrong codeword (early stop accepts any valid codeword) or oscillate
organs.human_prior: Gallager 1962 rediscovered by MacKay & Neal 1996; the ratio parametrisation and the two-sweep product trick are Neal's implementation choices

organs.mechanism: at every iteration the decoder can print: bits changed from the channel decision, current parity errors, log-likelihood of the tentative word, expected parity errors and expected log-likelihood under the posteriors, and the posterior entropy -- i.e. it exposes its own convergence as measurables
