organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the watcher lists are shrunk in place (a stable partition), so a long list with many satisfied clauses is still scanned; that is what the blocker mitigates
organs.human_prior: Chaff's two-literal watching (2001); the blocker literal is MiniSat 2.2's own

organs.human_name: analyze (264-360): seen[], pathC, the reason chain via reason(var(p)), out_learnt[0] = ~p; ccmin_mode 2 with abstractLevel and litRedundant; out_btlevel from the max level among the rest
organs.mechanism: starting from the conflict clause, mark its literals; literals from the current decision level are counted (pathC), older ones go into the learnt clause; walk the trail backwards to the most recent marked literal, resolve with its reason clause, repeat until exactly one current-level literal remains (the first unique implication point), which negated becomes the asserting literal; then remove literals implied by others in the clause (recursive redundancy check with a level bitmask as a fast filter); the backjump level is the highest level among the remaining literals, so the learnt clause is unit there
organs.input: a conflict clause; the trail; reasons
organs.output: a learnt clause and a backtrack level
assumptions: the first UIP gives short, quickly asserting clauses (empirically better than later cuts); minimisation pays for itself
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: every conflict yields a clause that forces a new assignment immediately after backjumping (non-chronological); the search never repeats the same failure
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the learnt clause length is unbounded; the DB reduction exists because of it
organs.human_prior: GRASP (Marques-Silva & Sakallah 1996) for learning; Chaff for first UIP; Sorensson & Biere 2009 for minimisation

organs.human_name: pickBranchLit (225-240): random_var_freq, order_heap.removeMin, polarity[]; Solver.h varBumpActivity / varDecayActivity (var_inc *= 1/var_decay; rescale at 1e100); analyze bumps every variable it sees
organs.mechanism: each variable carries an activity; every variable touched during conflict analysis is bumped by the current increment; instead of decaying all activities after each conflict the increment itself grows by 1/var_decay (rescaling everything when it overflows), which is the same ordering at O(1) cost; decisions pop the maximum-activity unassigned variable from a heap, with a small probability of a random variable instead; the literal's sign comes from the polarity vector
assumptions: variables recently involved in conflicts are the ones worth deciding on (locality of conflicts); recency should dominate frequency, hence exponential decay
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a decision heuristic that costs O(log n) per decision and adapts to the search
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with var_decay near 1 the heuristic becomes frequency-based and stale; the random picks exist to escape
organs.human_prior: Chaff's VSIDS (2001); the increment-growth trick is MiniSat's (Een & Sorensson 2003)

organs.human_name: reduceDB (525-545) with reduceDB_lt; search: learnts.size() - nAssigns() >= max_learnts; max_learnts *= learntsize_inc on the learntsize_adjust schedule; claBumpActivity / claDecayActivity
organs.mechanism: learnt clauses carry an activity bumped when they take part in a conflict; when the number of learnt clauses beyond the current assignment exceeds max_learnts, sort by activity (binary clauses last), delete the lower-activity half plus any below a threshold, never deleting binary clauses or clauses that are the reason for a current assignment; the limit starts at a fraction of the original clause count and grows geometrically on a schedule keyed to conflict counts
assumptions: most learnt clauses stop being useful; recent usefulness (activity) predicts future usefulness; the database may grow slowly forever
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: propagation stays fast as learning continues
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: activity is a poor proxy on some families (LBD replaced it in Glucose, 2009)
organs.human_prior: Chaff's deletion; the activity-based halving is MiniSat's

organs.human_name: solve_ (751-790): rest_base = luby(restart_inc, curr_restarts) or restart_inc^k; search(rest_base * restart_first); luby (734-743)
organs.mechanism: the search runs until a conflict budget is spent, then backtracks to level 0 (keeping every learnt clause and all activities) and starts again with a budget that follows the Luby sequence (1,1,2,1,1,2,4,...) times a base of 100 conflicts, or a geometric sequence if configured; because the state that matters (clauses, activities, polarities) survives, a restart is a re-ordering of decisions, not a fresh start
assumptions: run-time distributions of CDCL are heavy-tailed, so restarting with a universal (Luby) schedule bounds the expected time within a log factor of the optimal fixed cutoff (Luby, Sinclair, Zuckerman 1993)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: escapes from unlucky early decisions at no loss of learnt information
organs.human_prior: Gomes et al. 1998 (restarts for heavy tails); Huang 2007 (Luby in SAT)

organs.human_interpretation: the neuron whose weight vector is closest to the input wins
organs.mechanism: compute a distance (euclidean by default; cosine, manhattan, chebyshev, or a user callable) from x to every weight vector on the x*y lattice into activation_map, then argmin -> (i, j); nothing else in the file reads activation_map
assumptions: the distance is the right notion of similarity for the data
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the competition that makes the map a quantiser

organs.human_name: neighbourhood function (gaussian / mexican hat / bubble / triangle) on a rectangular or hexagonal grid
organs.human_interpretation: neighbours of the winner on the GRID (not in input space) are pulled too; this is what makes the map topology-preserving
organs.mechanism: precomputed grid coordinate arrays _xx, _yy (hexagonal: odd rows offset, meshgrid at construction); given the winner c and radius sigma return a (x, y) matrix of weights: gaussian exp(-d^2/2sigma^2) as an outer product of per-axis factors, mexican hat (gaussian times (1-d^2/sigma^2)), bubble (1 inside radius else 0), triangle (linear to 0 at sigma)
organs.output: an (x, y) matrix of coupling weights
assumptions: grid distance, not weight distance, defines who learns together
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: ordering: without it the map is plain competitive learning / k-means-like (record: 'fails to organise')
organs.source_boundary: neighborhood = one of _gaussian/_mexican_hat/_bubble/_triangle plus the coordinate arrays

organs.human_name: learning-rate and sigma schedule (five decay laws)
organs.mechanism: eta(t) and sigma(t) are pure functions of (initial, t, max_iter): inverse_decay_to_zero (C/(C+t), C=max_iter/100), linear_decay_to_zero, inverse_decay_to_one, linear_decay_to_one, asymptotic_decay (1/(1+t/(max_iter/2))); chosen by name at construction; t is the iteration or, with use_epochs, the epoch index
assumptions: the total budget max_iter is known in advance (every law is normalised by it)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a wide early radius orders the map, a narrow late radius refines it; the record names the schedule as the failure locus
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; by reading: sigma decaying below ~1 leaves neighbours uncoupled; a budget too short leaves the map twisted (record)

organs.human_name: Kohonen update rule w += eta * h(c, sigma) * (x - w)
organs.mechanism: one sample at a time: every weight vector moves toward x by the fraction eta * neighbourhood weight of its grid cell (einsum over the lattice)
assumptions: small steps; the sample order matters (see sequencing)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the only place the codebook changes in online training

organs.mechanism: per iteration: accumulate numerator += h(bmu(sample), sigma) * sample and denominator += h over ALL samples with the weights frozen, then w = (1 - lr) * w + lr * numerator/denominator for cells with denominator > 0 (untouched cells keep their weights)
organs.input: the whole data matrix, sigma(t), lr(t)
organs.update: once per pass over the data
assumptions: order-invariant by construction
cells no sample reaches never move
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: an alternative to the online rule; the record does not say which Techne's harness used
organs.source_boundary: train_batch_offline (the numba variant 786-874 is a duplicate)

organs.human_name: train() loop: sequential / shuffled / epoch order; fixed_points
organs.mechanism: _build_iteration_indexes yields sample indices: arange(n) % len(data) or tiled epochs, optionally shuffled by the seeded RandomState; train() walks them, computes the winner (or takes the caller's fixed (i, j) for that sample index), and calls update with the decay index t (iteration or epoch)
organs.output: a sequence of (sample, winner, t) events
assumptions: reusing samples cyclically is harmless
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: fixed_points is a supervised anchor: a sample can be pinned to a cell (semi-supervised SOM)

organs.mechanism: random: each cell takes a random data sample; pca: eigh of the data covariance, the lattice is laid on the plane of the top two eigenvectors around the data mean (linspace -1..1 per axis); the constructor otherwise draws uniform random weights normalised per cell
assumptions: pca: >= 2 features and a 2-D lattice
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the code claims pca init converges faster and is deterministic (571-576); not measured here
organs.source_boundary: the two *_init methods + constructor weight draw

organs.human_name: lmpar (1-264): parl / paru from the Gauss-Newton step and the gradient; the qrsolv iteration; 'abs(dxnorm-delta) .le. 0.1*delta' or 10 iterations
organs.mechanism: first solve the undamped (par = 0) least-squares step from the QR; if its scaled norm is within delta (10 percent slack) accept par = 0; else bracket par: a lower bound from the derivative of the step norm (parl, zero if the Jacobian is rank deficient) and an upper bound from the gradient norm over delta (paru); iterate at most 10 times: solve the damped system by qrsolv (a sequence of Givens rotations on R with sqrt(par) D appended), evaluate fp = ||D x|| - delta, stop if |fp| <= 0.1 delta, else take a Newton correction on 1/||D x||, update the bracket by the sign of fp, and set par = max(parl, par + parc)
organs.input: R, the permutation, Q'b, the scaling D, delta, the previous par
organs.output: par, x(par), and the Cholesky factor S
organs.state: none across calls except par as a warm start
assumptions: ||D x(par)|| is decreasing and convex in par (Hebden / More: so the Newton iteration on its reciprocal converges monotonically); 10 iterations and a 10 percent tolerance suffice because the outer loop tolerates an inexact radius
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the trust-region subproblem for least squares solved to 10 percent in a handful of cheap rotations rather than by an eigen-decomposition
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: rank-deficient Jacobians set parl = 0 and the exceptional-case exit accepts a step inside the region; the 10-iteration cap returns 'the best value obtained so far'
organs.human_prior: Hebden 1973; More 1978 'The Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm: implementation and theory' (the paper this code implements)

organs.human_name: lmder (330-440): actred, prered, dirder, ratio; 'if (ratio .gt. p25) go to 240'; temp = p5*dirder/(dirder + p5*actred); delta = pnorm/p5 on ratio >= 0.75; the info 1-8 tests
organs.mechanism: after a step p of scaled length pnorm: actual reduction = 1 - (fnorm1/fnorm)^2 (or -1 if the residual grew tenfold); predicted reduction from the linear model = ||J p||^2/fnorm^2 + 2 par pnorm^2/fnorm^2, directional derivative likewise; ratio = actual/predicted; if ratio <= 0.25 shrink delta to temp * min(delta, 10 pnorm) with temp from a quadratic interpolation of the residual along p (clamped to [0.1, 0.5]) and divide par by temp; if ratio >= 0.75 (or par = 0) set delta = 2 pnorm and halve par; accept the step only if ratio >= 1e-4; convergence tests on |actred| and prered (ftol), delta vs xtol ||D x||, and the scaled gradient (gtol); the first iteration caps delta at pnorm
organs.input: the step, the residual norms, par
assumptions: the quadratic model predicts the reduction well within delta; the actual/predicted ratio is a reliable measure of model quality (the trust-region premise)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: global convergence without a line search; the radius adapts to the model's local accuracy
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: constants (0.25, 0.75, 1e-4, factor 100 for the initial delta) are the paper's; a bad scaling D (mode 1 uses the Jacobian column norms) changes the geometry of delta
organs.human_prior: More 1978 section 4; the same acceptance rule is in every later trust-region code
organs.source_boundary: the inner loop of lmder (shared verbatim by lmdif and lmstr)

organs.human_name: dogleg (60-175): the Gauss-Newton solve from R packed by rows with a diagonal repair; qnorm <= delta -> return; sgnorm (the Cauchy step length); alpha from the boundary quadratic
organs.mechanism: solve R x = Q'b for the Gauss-Newton step (a zero diagonal entry is replaced by eps times the largest entry in its row: a cheap rank repair); if its scaled norm is within delta take it; else compute the scaled gradient and the Cauchy (steepest-descent minimiser) step length sgnorm; if sgnorm >= delta take the gradient step scaled to delta; else take the point on the segment from the Cauchy point to the Gauss-Newton point that lies on the boundary (alpha from a closed-form quadratic)
assumptions: the piecewise-linear dogleg path approximates the true trust-region minimiser well enough for the ratio test to accept most steps
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one triangular solve and a few norms per step; no damping parameter search
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the diagonal repair silently changes a singular system; the path is not the exact subproblem minimiser (Powell 1970 argued it need not be)
organs.human_prior: Powell 1970 'A hybrid method for nonlinear equations'

organs.human_name: hybrd (208-440): jeval, ncsuc / ncfail, nslow1 / nslow2, 'if (ncfail .eq. 2) go to 290', r1updt / r1mpyq; delta halved on ratio < 0.1, raised to 2 pnorm on ratio >= 0.5 or two successes
organs.mechanism: the Jacobian is formed by forward differences (fdjac1, banded if ml/mu say so) and QR-factored once per outer iteration; inside, each accepted step updates the factored Jacobian by the Broyden secant correction (a rank-one update of R carried through Q by Givens rotations, r1updt/r1mpyq) rather than re-evaluating; the outer loop re-evaluates only when two consecutive steps failed (ncfail = 2); progress monitors count iterations with actual reduction below 0.001 (nslow1, ten -> info 5) and Jacobian evaluations with reduction below 0.1 (nslow2, five -> info 4); delta is halved on ratio < 0.1 and raised on ratio >= 0.5 or after two successes
assumptions: secant information from accepted steps is good enough to avoid n function evaluations per iteration; failure to reduce the residual twice means the secant Jacobian has drifted
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: n-fold fewer function evaluations per iteration than a finite-difference Newton
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the monitors terminate with 'not making good progress' rather than diverging; the secant update can make R singular (r1updt reports sing; the dogleg's diagonal repair copes)
organs.source_boundary: hybrd's outer/inner loops (hybrj is the analytic-Jacobian twin)

organs.mechanism: state is kept as YH(i,j+1) = h^j y_i^(j) / j! for j = 0..NQ, i.e. the solution and its scaled Taylor coefficients at the current point, one column per order; a change of step size h -> rh*h is a column-wise rescale by rh^j (DSTODE 175-180); a change of order adds or drops a column; the array is also what the interpolant reads
organs.input: the accepted correction ACOR and the coefficients EL(j) after a successful step
organs.output: the current state for every consumer (predictor, error test, order change, interpolation, restart)
organs.update: per accepted step (470: YH(i,j) += EL(j)*ACOR(i)); rescaled on every h change
assumptions: the scaled derivatives are meaningful, i.e. the solution is smooth enough at the current order; the failure ladder (KFLAG <= -3) says explicitly when it stops trusting them
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one representation serves prediction, correction, error control, order change, step change and dense output; nothing is recomputed from past solution values
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: after repeated error-test failures the accumulated derivatives are assumed wrong and the array is truncated to order 1 with a fresh f evaluation (640-650); no measurement
organs.human_prior: Nordsieck (1962) representation chosen over storing past y values (the multistep textbook form); the choice is what makes step changes cheap
organs.source_boundary: every YH read/write in DSTODE; the LYH slice of RWORK in the driver

organs.mechanism: advance the history array to TN+H by NQ passes of in-place column additions YH1(I) += YH1(I+NYH) from the highest order down: multiplication by the Pascal-triangle matrix with no multiplications; the same loop with subtraction (440-445, 510-515) is the exact retraction used on failure
organs.output: predicted YH at TN+H (first column = predicted y)
assumptions: the Taylor form of YH (the organ above); exactness of the retraction relies on the additions being reversible in floating point only approximately (not measured)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the predictor costs ~N*NQ additions and no function evaluations

organs.mechanism: up to MAXCOR=3 iterations of either functional iteration (MITER=0: y <- y0 + el(1)*(h f(y) - yh2)) or the chord method (solve P dy = h f - (yh2 + acor) with P = I - h*el0*J held fixed); after each iteration the weighted norm DEL of the correction is taken and CRATE = max(0.2*CRATE, DEL/DELP) estimates the contraction rate; the stopping test is DEL*min(1, 1.5*CRATE) <= TESCO(2,NQ)*CONIT, i.e. the iteration is declared converged when its PREDICTED remaining error is below the local error test scale, not when the last correction is tiny; divergence (DEL > 2*DELP at M >= 2) aborts early
organs.input: predicted YH, the iteration matrix P (if chord), f
organs.output: the accumulated correction ACOR and the corrected y, or a convergence failure
organs.state: CRATE (persists across steps, reset to 0.7 when P is refreshed), DELP
assumptions: contraction is roughly geometric so one ratio predicts the tail
for the chord method P may be stale (it is deliberately reused; see the refresh policy organ)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the convergence test is calibrated to the error test, so no iterations are spent beyond what the step can use; CRATE lets a slow iteration stop early and trigger a matrix refresh instead of burning MAXCOR
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with MITER=0 on a stiff problem the iteration diverges for any step larger than ~1/|lambda| and the ladder shrinks h until the budget is exhausted (the record's failure)
organs.human_prior: MAXCOR=3 and the 0.2/1.5 constants are Hindmarsh's tuning; not derived

organs.mechanism: error weights EWT(i) = RTOL*|y_i| + ATOL(i) are recomputed from the current y before every step (driver 250-260) and inverted; every norm in the integrator is the RMS of v_i/EWT_i (DVNORM); the local error estimate is the norm of the accumulated correction divided by TESCO(2,NQ) (a method constant), and the step is accepted iff that is <= 1
organs.output: EWT vector; the scalar DSM; accept/reject
assumptions: a mixed relative/absolute tolerance is the right notion of close; components with EWT <= 0 are an illegal input (driver 510, ISTATE=-6)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one scalar drives every decision (convergence, acceptance, step and order choice), and it is dimensionless so the same constants serve every problem
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: TOLSF = uround * ||y||_EWT > 1 means the tolerance is below machine precision; the driver returns ISTATE=-2 (520) rather than loop

organs.mechanism: after a step (success or failure) three step-size multipliers are computed from error estimates at orders NQ-1, NQ, NQ+1: RH = 1/(c * D^(1/(q+1)) + tiny) with c = 1.3, 1.2, 1.4; the largest wins; a change is made only if RH >= 1.1 (else IALTH=3: do not look again for 3 steps); after any change IALTH = NQ+1 steps of hold-off; RMAX caps the increase at 10 (1e4 on the first step, 2 after a failure); on failure RHUP=0 (never raise order) and after two failures RH <= 0.2; the order-up estimate needs the previous step's correction, which is saved into the spare column only when IALTH=1
organs.input: DSM, ACOR, YH(:,L), the saved previous correction, KFLAG
organs.output: new H, new NQ (NQ-1, NQ, NQ+1)
organs.state: IALTH (hold-off counter), RMAX, the spare YH column
assumptions: the local error scales as h^(q+1) (the exponent in each ratio)
changing h or q costs a rescale and destabilises the estimates, hence the hold-off
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the step and order track the solution's smoothness without a fixed schedule; the hysteresis (1.1) and hold-off (IALTH) stop the controller chattering
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the constants 1.3/1.2/1.4 bias toward keeping or lowering order; an order increase is only ever tried from a clean step (RHUP=0 on failure)
organs.human_prior: the safety factors and the 1.1 threshold are tuning; the asymmetric bias against order increase is a design choice recorded in the code, not in the prologue

organs.mechanism: the iteration matrix P = I - h*el0*J is NOT rebuilt every step: RC tracks the ratio of the current h*el0 to the one P was built with; P is rebuilt when |RC-1| > CCMAX=0.3, or every MSBP=20 steps, or when the corrector fails to converge with a stale P (JCUR=0 -> refresh and retry the same step before reducing h); refreshing resets CRATE to 0.7
organs.state: RC, NSLP (step of last build), JCUR
organs.update: per step and per convergence failure
assumptions: J changes slowly along the solution; a wrong P only slows the chord iteration, it does not change the fixed point
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the expensive operation (N function evaluations or a user Jacobian plus an LU) is amortised over ~20 steps; a convergence failure is first blamed on staleness, then on the step
organs.human_prior: CCMAX=0.3, MSBP=20 are tuning constants set in the driver (opkdmain.f 110-118)
organs.source_boundary: the IPUP/RC/NSLP/JCUR variables and their tests

organs.mechanism: five ways to build and apply P = I - h*el0*J behind one interface: 1 user dense Jacobian; 2 finite-difference dense (N extra f calls, increment R = max(sqrt(uround)*|y_j|, r0/EWT_j) with r0 = 1000*|h|*uround*N*||f||); 3 a DIAGONAL approximation from ONE extra f call along the predicted correction direction (a diagonal Jacobian-vector estimate; the solve is a vector divide, rescaled when h*el0 changes without a rebuild, DSOLSY 300-390); 4 user banded; 5 finite-difference banded (MBAND extra f calls, columns grouped by band); dense/banded go through LINPACK LU (DGEFA/DGBFA) and back-solve
organs.output: P factored in WM, or IERPJ
organs.state: WM (the factored matrix; for MITER=3 the diagonal and the h*el0 it was built at)
assumptions: for MITER=3 the diagonal approximation is only good when J is nearly diagonal in the EWT scaling; the code cannot tell and the corrector rate (CRATE) is the only signal
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: cost/accuracy of the Newton matrix is a user choice orthogonal to the integrator (DSTODE is independent of MITER, prologue)

organs.mechanism: convergence failure: refresh P if stale, else retract, RMAX=2, h*0.25, count NCF; at MXNCF=10 or h=HMIN -> KFLAG=-2. error-test failure: retract, KFLAG-1, choose h at order NQ or NQ-1 with RHUP=0; after 2 failures h <= 0.2*h; after 3 the history is distrusted: order -> 1, f re-evaluated, h*0.1, IALTH=5; at 10 failures or h=HMIN -> KFLAG=-1. driver: MXSTEP (default 500) steps per call -> ISTATE=-1 with the partial solution returned; T+H == T in floating point -> a warning up to MXHNIL=10 times, then silence, integration continues
organs.output: a retry with a smaller h and/or lower order, or a typed failure return with the state as of the last good step
assumptions: the last accepted state is always recoverable (retraction is exact enough); failures are local, so shrinking h is the right first move
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: every failure is typed (-1 budget, -2 precision, -4 error test, -5 corrector, -6 weights) and returns the solution as far as it got with the offending component (IWORK(16)) named; nothing is silently wrong
organs.failure_landscape: the record's own: a non-stiff method on a stiff problem exhausts MXSTEP (ISTATE=-1) rather than diverging; the ladder makes the failure cheap and legible
organs.human_prior: the retreat factors 0.25 / 0.2 / 0.1 and the counts 10 / 10 / 500 are tuning

organs.mechanism: if the user gives no H0: TOL = max(RTOL, ATOL/|y|) clipped to [100*uround, 1e-3]; H0 = 1/sqrt(1/(TOL*W0^2) + TOL*||f||_EWT^2) with W0 = max(|T|,|TOUT|); capped by |TOUT-T| and HMAX; then RMAX=1e4 lets the first accepted step grow fast
assumptions: a first step that is too small is cheap to recover from (RMAX=1e4 on the first step), so the heuristic errs small
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: removes a user parameter; the two terms balance a time-scale bound and a derivative bound

organs.human_name: DCFODE (Adams to order 12, BDF to order 5)
organs.mechanism: the integration coefficients EL(1..q+1) and the three test constants TESCO(1..3,q) for every order are generated at run time from the coefficients of the product polynomial (x+1)(x+2)...(x+q-1) built by an integer-like recurrence; Adams: integrate the polynomial (PINT, XPIN); BDF: normalise by PC(2); the maximum orders (12, 5) are hard limits of the tables
assumptions: BDF above order 5 is unstable (the human record's reason for MXORDS=5); the table size encodes that prior
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no stored tables; the same code serves two method families
organs.human_prior: the two families and their order caps

organs.mechanism: the k-th derivative at any T in [TN-HU, TN] is read off the history array by a Horner-like sum over the columns with s = (T-TN)/H and falling-factorial coefficients; no extra f calls; T outside the last step is refused (IFLAG)
assumptions: the history polynomial is accurate over the last step only
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: output at user times decoupled from the step sequence (ITASK=1 interpolates rather than stepping to TOUT)

organs.human_name: DSTODA method switch (DLSODA), read in part
organs.mechanism: (DLSODA only) after each converged corrector the contraction rate is turned into a local Lipschitz-constant estimate PDEST = max(PDEST, RATE/|h*el(1)|); every ICOUNT steps the code computes the step the OTHER family could take (a stability-bounded step for Adams, SM1(NQ)/PDH; an error-bounded step for BDF) and switches only if the other family's step is at least RATIO=5 times larger; a switch resets order and rescales YH
organs.update: per step; decision every ICOUNT steps
assumptions: the corrector's contraction rate is a usable proxy for the spectral radius of h*J (a stiffness detector with no eigenvalue computation)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: removes the user's MF choice -- the record's failure mode (wrong family for the problem) is what this organ exists to prevent
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; by reading the RATIO=5 hysteresis prevents flapping but delays the switch

organs.mechanism: for each sample k: y = w . x[k]; e = d[k] - y; w += learning_rule(e, x[k]); w_history[k] = w before the update; init_weights draws random or zeros or takes a vector
assumptions: a linear-in-parameters model w . x
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: UNKNOWN
